outline: Biostatistics, Epidemiology/Population Health, & Interpretation of the Medical Literature
Clinical decision making — application of study results to patient care
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Diagnostic threshold tradeoff on a receiver operating characteristic curve
mechanism: For a continuous diagnostic test in which values above a cutoff are called positive, lowering the positivity threshold classifies more tested patients as positive. This increases sensitivity and decreases the false-negative rate, but decreases specificity and increases the false-positive rate. On an ROC plot with sensitivity on the vertical axis and 1-specificity on the horizontal axis, the operating point therefore moves upward and to the right.
vignette: A quantitative plasma assay is being evaluated as an aid to diagnosing pulmonary embolism in adults who present to an emergency department with compatible symptoms. Every participant undergoes both the assay and an independent reference-standard evaluation. The investigators construct a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve for the assay. Clinicians decide that, for its intended diagnostic role, they want to reduce the number of affected patients who have a negative assay result. They therefore lower the assay value that is considered positive.
lead: Which of the following changes is expected as a direct result of lowering the positivity threshold?
correct: Sensitivity increases, specificity decreases, and the operating point moves upward and to the right on the ROC curve
distractors: Sensitivity decreases, specificity increases, and the operating point moves downward and to the left on the ROC curve
Sensitivity increases, specificity increases, and the operating point moves upward and to the left on the ROC curve
Sensitivity decreases, specificity decreases, and the operating point moves downward and to the right on the ROC curve
Sensitivity remains unchanged, specificity decreases, and the operating point moves to the right without a vertical change on the ROC curve
distractor_notes: This is the direction expected when the positivity threshold is raised, not lowered: fewer results are called positive, so sensitivity falls while specificity rises.
Changing only the decision threshold of the same continuous test ordinarily trades sensitivity against specificity; lowering the threshold does not increase both simultaneously.
Lowering the threshold causes more, not fewer, diseased participants to test positive, so sensitivity should rise rather than fall.

Lowering the threshold changes the fraction of diseased participants classified as positive as well as the fraction of nondiseased participants classified as positive; sensitivity therefore does not remain fixed.
key_expl: Lowering the positive cutoff makes it easier for a result to be labeled positive. Among participants who truly have disease, more will test positive, so sensitivity rises and the false-negative rate falls. Among participants who do not have disease, more will also test positive, so specificity falls and the false-positive rate rises. Because an ROC curve plots sensitivity on the y-axis and 1-specificity (the false-positive rate) on the x-axis, both coordinates increase and the operating point moves upward and to the right.
objective: Apply the diagnostic-threshold tradeoff: lowering the positive cutoff of a continuous test increases sensitivity and the false-positive rate while decreasing specificity and the false-negative rate; on an ROC plot of sensitivity versus 1-specificity, the operating point moves upward and to the right.
clues: goal is fewer affected patients with negative results

sources.date: AHRQ Methods Guide, June 2012; authoritative methodological guidance verified 2026-08-28
sources.locator: Appendix — Test Performance Metrics, Sensitivity and Specificity, page A-1; receiver operating characteristic discussion immediately following
sources.support: AHRQ defines sensitivity and specificity and states that for a continuously valued test, raising the threshold decreases sensitivity and increases specificity, whereas lowering the threshold increases sensitivity and decreases specificity. It also describes the ROC curve as sensitivity plotted against 1-specificity across thresholds.
